newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Albright says strong Europe is good for U.S..
newsitem.headline: Albright says strong Europe is good for U.S..

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, recalling her past as a child of divided Europe, said on Tuesday she looked forward to helping make the continent "whole and free again".

Speaking to the European Commission -- the European Union's executive -- Czech-born Albright said the expansion of the EU and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) should be carried out with respect.

Nikolaus van der Pas, chief spokesman for the Commission, quoted Albright as saying EU membership for central and eastern European nations "should not be seen as a consolation prize for non-NATO membership".
"She stressed the importance of the process of enlargement and stressed the process should be respectful," he said.
"She recalled that she was a child of a divided Europe and that she was looking forward to helping make the continent whole and free again," he added.

Van der Pas said Albright discussed a wide range of issues with Commission President Jacques Santer, Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and Hans van den Broek, Emma Bonino and Yves-Thibault de Silguy, respectively responsible for external relations, humanitarian affairs and finance.
Albright told the Commission that the U.S. and EU had a great deal in common and that President Bill Clinton wanted a stronger relationship.

Despite divisions over Washington's controversial Helms-Burton Act, van der Pas quoted Albright as saying she wanted to see the much-vaunted New Transatlantic Agenda -- the informal agreement that governs relations between the EU and U.S. -- made more visible.

Van der Pas said Brittan raised the issue of Helms-Burton with Albright, saying he hoped discussions could continue on the subject regardless of whether a World Trade Organisation disputes panel on the issue is formed on Thursday as expected.

The EU and U.S. have been at odds over the act for almost a year. Among other things, it allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreigners deemed to have gained from investments in property confiscated by the Cuban government since the Communist revolution of 1959.

Albright was quoted as telling the commissioners that it was important for the U.S. to have a secular Turkey "rooted in the West", and added too that she hoped 1997 could herald a breakthrough in Ankara's relations with Greece as well as movement on solving the Cyprus problem.
On the Middle East, Albright said the EU and Washington's roles were "complimentary", but she stressed the U.S. "intended remaining at the centre as an honest broker".
De Silguy told Albright he wanted the EU to develop closer consultation in monetary and economic matters with the U.S.
Van der Pas said de Silguy had particularly requested more consultation over macro-economic issues such as capital transfers.
Albright had replied that she hoped this could be discussed in more depth at the U.S.-European Union summit in May in the Netherlands.
